newsitem.title: UK: SIA advances start of 2nd Dublin cargo flight.
newsitem.headline: SIA advances start of 2nd Dublin cargo flight.

text.p: Singapore Airlines has brought forward the start-up date for its second weekly cargo flight to Dublin as a result of pent-up demand, said SIA cargo manager for the UK and Ireland Barry Gibson.

The Wednesday flight was originally scheduled to start with the summer timetable in April but will now commence on Wednesday March 5 with with another Boeing 747-400 freighter capable of carrying up to 120 tonnes.
Most of the traffic is electronics with Ireland increasingly becoming a key country in the supply chain of the global electronics industry, he added.
SIA started its first freighter flight to Dublin and Copenhagen via Dubai in October. This routes Singapore-Dubai-Dublin-Copenhagen-Dubai-Singapore.
Uplift from Dublin would be six main deck pallets or 15 to 20 tonnes. SIA expects to unload some 40 tonnes in Dublin and 60 tonnes in Copenhagen from each flight.
Return flights take some 20 percent from Dublin and 70 percent from Copenhagen. This breakdown is not rigid and Gibson said all SIA flights have been filled.
Dubai is normally little more than a refuelling stop, Gibson said.
Apart from the regular traffic in electronics, Gibson said SIA had flown racehorses from Dublin to Dubai. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
